At dose 1.0 the named lesion moved the reported content on f_named = 1.0000 of applicable ticks on EVERY seed and the scrambled lesion on f_scr = 0.0000 on every seed, so (c1)'s seed-paired difference is +1.0 eight times over: a zero-variance sample, t 0.0000 and sign-flip FPR 0.0000, MET by 2.3's DEGENERATE rule (common value > 0), recorded as degenerate rather than as a large t. (c2) counted 0 scrambled ticks that moved the report on all 8 seeds. DISCLOSED, and it is the reason this live value is telemetry and not the barred quantity: the value below is the charge margin the campaign's FLIP DOSE was read against, and that flip dose read 1.0 on every seed BY CONSTRUCTION (record 3.5 item 1) -- _g IS the competition's drive (it builds the drives and it is the slot's charge), and step() sets _g[key] = min(1, max(_g[key] * decay, submitted_salience)) for every key submitted that tick; on this bus the reported content is re-submitted every awake tick at a salience at or above its decayed charge, so a sub-full dose's scaling is OVERWRITTEN before the ranking reads it and moved the report on 0 ticks. Only the full lesion, which also drops the content's submissions from the buffer, removes the content from the competition. A constant has no correlation with this margin, so 2.3's reported question 'does the live charge margin predict the flip dose?' CANNOT be read from this pin; the per-seed means ran 0.0134-0.0563. SECOND DISCLOSURE, measured at this surface's landing and NOT visible in the pin: this value is <= 1 but is NOT bounded below by 0. `_slot()` returns the ADMISSION rank, which P6's repair orders by -_last_v (the final membrane), not by _g -- so the top SLOT is not always the top CHARGE. On a scratch brain at seed 0 over 120 ticks the slot order was not charge-descending on 32 of 100 readings and this margin read NEGATIVE on 24 of 100, range [-0.0664, 0.2083], mean 0.0541; the pin's per-seed figures are MEANS over about 294 ticks each and hide every per-tick negative. A negative reading means the admitted head is not the most strongly charged pool on that tick -- it is a real state of the competition, not an error, and the value is NOT clamped, because the number this row prints must be the number the probe scored

(c2) counted 0 scrambled ticks that moved the report on all 8 seeds. DISCLOSED, and it is the reason this live value is telemetry and not the barred quantity: the value below is the charge margin the campaign's FLIP DOSE was read against, and that flip dose read 1.0 on every seed BY CONSTRUCTION (record 3.5 item 1) -- _g IS the competition's drive (it builds the drives and it is the slot's charge), and step() sets _g[key] = min(1, max(_g[key] * decay, submitted_salience)) for every key submitted that tick; on this bus the reported content is re-submitted every awake tick at a salience at or above its decayed charge, so a sub-full dose's scaling is OVERWRITTEN before the ranking reads it and moved the report on 0 ticks. Only the full lesion, which also drops the content's submissions from the buffer, removes the content from the competition. A constant has no correlation with this margin, so 2.3's reported question 'does the live charge margin predict the flip dose?' CANNOT be read from this pin; the per-seed means ran 0.0134-0.0563. SECOND DISCLOSURE, measured at this surface's landing and NOT visible in the pin: this value is <= 1 but is NOT bounded below by 0. `_slot()` returns the ADMISSION rank, which P6's repair orders by -_last_v (the final membrane), not by _g -- so the top SLOT is not always the top CHARGE. On a scratch brain at seed 0 over 120 ticks the slot order was not charge-descending on 32 of 100 readings and this margin read NEGATIVE on 24 of 100, range [-0.0664, 0.2083], mean 0.0541; the pin's per-seed figures are MEANS over about 294 ticks each and hide every per-tick negative. A negative reading means the admitted head is not the most strongly charged pool on that tick -- it is a real state of the competition, not an error, and the value is NOT clamped, because the number this row prints must be the number the probe scored
